rules.statement: Don't ask a pull request to edit, delete or disable a file the shared project template owns; when it has a defect, ask for an upstream issue on the template repository, and first check whether one is already tracked.
rules.why: The next template update restores any local edit or deletion of a template-owned file, so the fix belongs upstream.
rules.check: Before reporting a defect in a file, check whether the project template owns it (for example, it is managed through .copier-answers.yml or the template's instructions). If it does, phrase the fix as an upstream report. Don't report it when the pull request or the file already references an upstream issue.

rules.statement: A pull request description mentions every configuration change that alters behavior contributors will notice, such as a new .editorconfig file-header template or a new analyzer severity.
rules.why: Otherwise readers aren't told that their editors will start offering or flagging something new, for example a license header on every new C# file.
rules.check: Compare the changes to .editorconfig, analyzer severities and template answers in the diff against the pull request description and changelog. Report any change with a visible effect that neither one mentions.

rules.statement: Wrap Markdown prose at the width the file already uses (about 120 columns), and indent a list item's continuation lines under it.
rules.why: Inconsistent wrapping is harder to read and makes diffs harder to review.
rules.check: Look for added or edited Markdown lines that run well past the wrap width of the surrounding lines.
